page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-8GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 100 GB of local SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core profile, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top tier. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and large-block memory write bandwidth fall into the bottom 25%, while the overall PassMark memory score ranks in the bottom 10%. This indicates that while individual task execution on a single thread is highly efficient, concurrent multi-threaded workloads and heavy memory-write operations face performance bottlenecks.

Given its shared CPU allocation and balanced resource distribution, this server offers a cost-effective option for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated multi-core execution. It is well-suited for light web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, and basic development environments, but is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or complex multi-threaded applications.
